question: Which of the following metals can displace aluminium from an aluminium sulphate solution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aluminium **is a **highly reactive **metal and can be displaced by metals that are **more reactive** than it in a solution containing **aluminium sulphate.**
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** is **more reactive** than aluminium and can **displace** it from an aluminium sulphate solution.
 
• Mercury (Hg) is not a suitable option as it is a** liquid metal **and** less reactive** than aluminium.
 
• Iron (Fe) and Copper (Cu) are **less reactive** than aluminium and **cannot displace** it from an aluminium sulphate solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Magnesium** is a highly reactive metal and can react vigorously with many substances, including **water and acids.**
 
• **Mercury **is a liquid metal at room temperature and is commonly used in** thermometers, barometers**, and other scientific instruments.
 
• **Iron** is a relatively **abundant metal** and is used extensively in** construction, manufacturing, and transportation** industries.
 
• **Copper** is a highly** conductive metal** and is used in a variety of applications, including **electrical wiring and plumbing systems.**
